normative_proposal_semantics:
`GET /v1/apps/{appId}/gameplay/reward-receipts/{operationId}` has no request body.
`request` in receipt.schema.json validates the decoded operationId path component;
appId uses G1 UUID validation and account comes exclusively from authentication.
Authorize app membership, original operation owner and current resource visibility
on every read. Never enumerate or return another account's result. The endpoint
is an authorized primary read and uses private/no-store caching.

HTTP 200 `not_found` means no accepted completion receipt was observable at the
read boundary. It NEVER permits reidentification, a fresh sequence, replay grants,
or treating an uncertain operation as rejected. Use existing G1 terminal recovery
for uncertain/terminally rejected commands. HTTP 200 `completion_recorded` with
required `reward:null` means the retained completion was committed without a grant;
it is not a promised future reward. Non-null reward is a permanent grant receipt.
A stored accepted completion whose required reward evidence is missing returns
503 dependency/error, never null/not_found. Auth failures use G1 401/403, invalid
path 400, inaccessible resource 404, unsupported accepted operation type 409;
all application errors use the frozen G1 error envelope. Error code additions
`reward_receipt_integrity_unavailable` and `not_gameplay_completion` are semantic
keys, respectively dependency/retryable and conflict/nonretryable.

Use G1 explicit MessagePack/diagnostic-JSON negotiation and all G1 size/depth,
duplicate-key, UTF-8 and allocation limits. No decode fallback. The path UUID
is textual; response operationId/originatingOperationId/grantId are bin16 RFC
order on MessagePack, UUID text on JSON. feedRevision and quantities are checked
signed64 integers / TS bigint / C# long, decimal strings in JSON. Versions and
lineIndex are bounded int32; recordedAt/expiresAt use G1 integer epoch millis.
All other fields are strings, bool-free status tags, arrays/maps or explicit null
as the schema declares. Max 64 resolved lines and 256 KiB hard response including
envelope. Mutation planning must reject a receipt/group that cannot fit the G1
64 KiB committed group budget; this endpoint cannot justify oversized mutations.

All declared fields are required, unknown fields rejected, only reward and
entitlement expiresAt allow null. Unknown status/kind/schemaVersion fails closed.
Absent reward is invalid. No optional extension bag or arbitrary grant payload.
No pagination: one operation resolves to at most one grant in this bounded slice.
Future multiple reward slots require another reviewed schema/version.

## Business source, atomicity and reconciliation

BE-024 preserves the approved completion identity `(backend, app, account, mode,
session)`. That is operation-independent, but DOES NOT establish first-clear
eligibility. A reviewed game policy must resolve an immutable `eligibilityKey`
for the relevant occurrence: session-based and content-first-clear policies are
different and must never be inferred from the transport identity.

Proposed source key bytes are G1 canonical semantic framing `gsc1` applied to
the ordered string array `["gameplay.completion", policyId,
minimalDecimal(policyVersion), lowercaseAppUuid, mode, eligibilityKey]`;
`source.key` is lowercase SHA-256 of those bytes. The backend/account partition
is supplied from verified context; uniqueness is non-null canonical player,
source.kind, source.key, rewardSlot. policyId/version/eligibilityKey/rewardSlot
come only from reviewed server policy, never request fields. A policy-version
upgrade MUST preserve previous source identity/eligibility or migrate explicitly;
changing policy/version must not make prior first clears eligible again.
This encoding is a proposal requiring owner review, not approval of any policy.

grantId is new UUIDv7. planId/version and each definitionVersion are resolved and
pinned once; random choices, if a later approved plan has any, are fixed once.
lineIndex equals its zero-based array position. Separate lines can grant the same
currency/item; dedupe by grant + lineIndex, never by resource ID. Quantities are
strictly positive checked signed64; expiry is trusted server output.
Receipt values describe historical grant effects, not current spendable balances
or rights. Later consumption/revocation does not rewrite the historical receipt.

originatingOperationId identifies the first operation that committed the grant;
the outer operationId is the operation being looked up. Different accepted
operation IDs for the same eligible business source return the SAME grantId,
source, plan, lines and original feedRevision, without creating another reward.
No client-selected operation ID can establish source eligibility.

BE-024 must atomically commit completion, operation terminal result, business grant,
Wallet/Inventory/Entitlements changes, feed group and validated outbox event in the
application transaction; BE-022 borrows it. Lookup joins retained authorized
completion-to-grant correlation. SQL proposal/migration numbering belongs to
BE-004/022/024; this wire proposal applies no migration. Existing receipts must
survive deployment rollback; disable the new route before older handlers run,
retain immutable data and existing G1 terminal recovery. No receipt erasure or
historical reward backfill is authorized.

feedRevision is grant-group correlation, never a pull cursor or checkpoint.
Persist receipt presentation dedupe separately from pending outbox/projections.
Show accepted-awaiting-pull until ordered private pull (or complete authorized
snapshot reconciliation) incorporates the group. Never add receipt quantity to
confirmed value. Namespace all lookups/caches by backend/app/account; discard
stale-account callbacks, preserve that account's pending work. A replayed receipt
does not demonstrate current app permission or unexpired entitlement.

## Compatibility and review blockers

Old `0.2.0-core-schema.1` clients keep exactly their existing command/result/feed
contracts. New clients use this additive endpoint only after explicit supported
capability/configuration; 404/501 is unavailable, never synthesized receipt success.
SchemaVersion 1 here belongs solely to the new receipt operation. No change to
G1 operation schemaVersion, fingerprintVersion, collection enum or required
bootstrap collection. Synchronization must assign the final canonical version,
mirror hashes and deliberate codec/SDK rollout after review. G2 core codec proof
does not imply this proposal's runtime compatibility; its codec fixtures follow
only after approval.

Unresolved activation gates: EXT-GAME-OUTCOME-POLICY, DEC-CONTENT-VALIDATION,
DEC-LEGACY-TRUST, actual content/version mapping, validated proof tier, eligibility
occurrence and reward slot, trusted plan/binding configuration. Client signature
text is not proof. No reward for historical imported progress. Until actual
policy approval and BE-023 validation exist, reward-bearing gameplay stays
unavailable. Schema approval cannot authorize a test +1 grant or bypass these.

Required G2 reviews: backend contract owner and client contract/consumer roles
approve route necessity, source encoding, absent/null/enum/rollout semantics and
fixture mappings; no reviewer signature or approval is claimed here.
review_amendments: This approved operation replaces proposal/unapproved wording only within this pinned scope. Historical proposal evidence remains unapproved provenance.

source.policyId and source.policyVersion identify an immutable eligibility namespace, not the currently deployed evaluator version. Routine evaluation-rule upgrades retain that namespace. An explicit migration must preserve existing source keys/grants and map prior eligibility before activation; changing the hash input is not an idempotency strategy. Evaluator/plan versions remain separate server configuration.

Eligibility key is a server-resolved nonempty Unicode scalar string of at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes; reject lone surrogates. Preserve scalar bytes without NFC or case normalization. policyId and mode obey the G1 semanticKey rule; version is minimal decimal 1..2147483647; app UUID is canonical lowercase RFC text. Framing is gsc1 followed by canonical ordered array/string tags, no separators between array elements. Do not use the command fingerprint API as this array algorithm.

Advertise capability through explicit trusted client composition/configuration pinned with the service deployment until a separately reviewed capability endpoint exists. Do not add fields to closed G1 bootstrap/error schemas. Missing capability or 404/501 means unavailable.
A completion and its optional grant must preserve durable immutable correlation; integrity failure is a retryable dependency error, never a fabricated null or not_found.
Schema-only approval. No production endpoint/DTO/codecs, business-source runtime implementation, reward policy, historical replay, device or G3 approval is supplied.

client_field_mappings.operationId,originatingOperationId,grant: wire UUID bin16 RFC order; C# Guid; TS branded UUID; domain and SQL distinct
client_field_mappings.feedRevision,quantity: C# long / TS bigint / SQL bigint; diagnostic decimal string; feedRevision is correlation only
client_field_mappings.recordedAt,expiresAt: bounded integer Unix milliseconds; expiresAt explicitly nullable
client_field_mappings.protocolVersion,schemaVersion,policyVers: bounded C# int / TS number; lineIndex equals array position
client_field_mappings.status,kind,source.key,source.rewardSlot: explicit named string fields; closed discriminated union, reject unknown fields/status/version
client_field_mappings.reward: required nullable receipt only for completion_recorded; forbidden for not_found
client_field_mappings.lines: 1..64 typed currency/item_stack/entitlement lines; historical effects never added to confirmed projections

minimal_consumer_scope: CL-105/107/108 and INT-008/010 reuse unchanged G1 profile/wallet/inventory-stack/entitlement/progression bootstrap/pull shapes. Catalog definitions, binding and version resolution stay server-owned BE-017; no catalog browsing, instances, spend, claim or commerce API approval.
